source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 17 (PDF 85-117, printed 81-113); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 17 (Alternating Current), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 An alternating current is a current that:

options.text: flows in one direction with constant value
flows in one direction in pulses

blocks.explanation: AC means a sinusoidally varying current, represented by sine or cosine functions of time (17.1).

book_ref.quote: An alternating current AC means a sinusoidally varying current

blocks.prompt: 2 In the equation V = Vₒ sin ωt, the symbol ω represents the:

options.text: angular frequency of the alternating voltage

blocks.explanation: Vₒ is the maximum voltage and ω is the angular frequency of the alternating voltage (17.1).

book_ref.quote: Vₒ represents maximum value of voltage and ω is the angular frequency

blocks.prompt: 3 In an alternating current, the direction of current reverses after every:
blocks.explanation: The direction of current reverses after every half-cycle (17.1).

book_ref.quote: the direction of current reverses after every half-cycle

blocks.prompt: 4 An alternating voltage changes most rapidly:
blocks.explanation: Changes occur most rapidly at the zero crossover points and most slowly at the peak (17.1).

book_ref.quote: changes occur most rapidly at the zero (crossover) points and most slowly at its peak

blocks.prompt: 5 One complete set of positive and negative values of an alternating quantity is called:
blocks.explanation: One complete set of positive and negative values is a cycle (17.1).

book_ref.quote: One complete set of positive and negative values of an alternating quantity is called a cycle.

blocks.prompt: 6 The path traced by an alternating quantity plotted against time is called its:
blocks.explanation: The waveform is the path traced by an alternating quantity plotted against a variable such as time (17.1).

book_ref.quote: The path traced by an alternating quantity

blocks.prompt: 7 An alternating voltage completes one cycle in 0.025 s. Its frequency is:

book_ref.quote: The unit of frequency is hertz (Hz); where 1 Hz = 1 cycle per second

blocks.prompt: 8 AC is preferred over DC for supply between cities because AC:

options.text: can be transferred over long distances without much energy loss
can be stored easily in batteries

blocks.explanation: The box says AC is easily transferred over long distances without much energy loss, while DC loses power (17.1).

book_ref.quote: AC is easy to be transferred over longer distances

blocks.prompt: 9 The average value of a sinusoidal alternating voltage over one complete cycle is:
blocks.explanation: Over a full cycle the positive and negative half-cycles cancel, so the average is zero (17.1).

book_ref.quote: If we calculate the average of a complete sine wave over a full cycle (0 to 2π), the result is zero

blocks.prompt: 10 The average value of an AC waveform is usually taken over:
blocks.explanation: Since the full-cycle average is zero, the average value usually means the average over one half-cycle (17.1).

book_ref.quote: we usually mean the average over one half-cycle (0 to π)

blocks.prompt: 11 The peak value of a full-wave rectified sine voltage is 200 V. Its average value is:
blocks.explanation: Vₐᵥ = 0.637 Vₒ = 0.637 × 200 V = 127.4 V (17.1). 141.4 V would be the rms value.

book_ref.quote: For a full-wave rectified sine wave, the average values of current and voltage are given by

blocks.prompt: 12 The average value of an AC waveform is mainly used in situations involving:
blocks.explanation: The average value is used with rectification, where the output is pulsating DC (17.1).

book_ref.quote: The average value is used in situations involving rectification.

blocks.prompt: 13 The highest value that an AC waveform reaches during one cycle is its:
blocks.explanation: Peak or maximum value is the highest value reached during one cycle, written Vₒ or Iₒ (17.1).

book_ref.quote: It is the highest value that an AC waveform reaches during one cycle.

blocks.prompt: 14 A sinusoidal voltage has a peak value of 170 V. Its peak-to-peak value is:
blocks.explanation: For a symmetrical sine wave Vp-p = 2Vₒ = 2 × 170 V = 340 V (17.1).

book_ref.quote: This is the total distance from the positive peak to the negative peak of the waveform.

blocks.prompt: 15 An alternating voltage is V = 100 sin ωt volt. Its instantaneous value when ωt = 30° is:

book_ref.quote: The value of an AC quantity at any instant of time is known as instantaneous value.

blocks.prompt: 16 A non-contact voltage detector (pen tester) detects AC under a carpet by sensing the:

options.text: electromagnetic field generated by the current

blocks.explanation: Non-contact detectors sense the electromagnetic field produced by the current and show it by light or sound (17.1).

book_ref.quote: we can use a non-contact voltage detector, known as a pen tester

blocks.prompt: 17 The rms value of an alternating current is the value of a constant current that produces in a resistor the same:
blocks.explanation: rms current is the constant current giving the same power (heating effect) in a resistor as the AC (17.1).

book_ref.quote: The value of a constant current that produces the same power in a resistor as the alternating current.

blocks.prompt: 18 The peak value of the mains voltage is 311 V. Its rms value is about:
blocks.explanation: Vrms = 0.707 Vₒ = 0.707 × 311 V ≈ 220 V (17.1). 198 V is 0.637 Vₒ, the half-cycle average.

book_ref.quote: So, rms current, Iᵣₘₛ is equal to 0.707 Iₒ

blocks.prompt: 19 An AC ammeter reads an rms current of 5 A. The peak current is:

book_ref.quote: The value of a constant voltage that produces the same power in a resistor as the alternating voltage.

blocks.prompt: 20 The hissing sound near high voltage power lines is mainly caused by:

options.text: corona discharge (ionisation of the surrounding air)

blocks.explanation: Corona discharge: the strong electric field ionises the air around the conductor, giving glow, radio noise and hissing (17.1).

book_ref.quote: The hissing sound often heard near high voltage power lines is primarily caused by corona discharge

blocks.prompt: 21 A current is identified as alternating if it:
blocks.explanation: If the current periodically reverses direction it is AC; if it flows in a single direction it is DC (17.1).

book_ref.quote: If the current periodically reverses direction, it is alternating current.

blocks.text: 17.2 Relation Between Mean Power and Maximum Power for an Alternating Current

blocks.prompt: 22 A resistive load is one that:

options.text: stores energy in a magnetic field
does not store energy and simply dissipates it as heat
stores energy in an electric field
returns all energy to the source

blocks.explanation: A resistive load does not store energy like a capacitor or inductor; it dissipates energy as heat (17.2).

book_ref.quote: A resistive load is one that does not store energy

blocks.prompt: 23 The instantaneous power in an AC circuit is given by:

options.text: P = VI, with V and I the instantaneous values

blocks.explanation: Instantaneous power P = VI, where V and I are the instantaneous voltage and current (17.2).

book_ref.quote: The instantaneous power P in a circuit is the power at any given moment in time t.

blocks.prompt: 24 The peak power in a resistor carrying sinusoidal AC is 1200 W. The mean power is:

book_ref.quote: the mean power Pₘₑₐₙ is the average power over one complete cycle of the AC waveform

blocks.prompt: 25 The maximum power in a resistor R carrying an alternating current of peak value Iₒ is:
blocks.explanation: Pₘₐₓ = Iₒ²R (Eq. 17.6) (17.2).

book_ref.quote: then the maximum or peak power Pₘₐₓ is given by

blocks.prompt: 26 An rms current of 2 A flows through a 25 Ω resistor. The mean power is:
blocks.explanation: Pₘₑₐₙ = Iᵣₘₛ²R = (2 A)² × 25 Ω = 100 W (17.2).

book_ref.quote: Also we have expression for the mean power Pₘₑₐₙ represented by

blocks.prompt: 27 The mean power in a resistive load is only half the peak power because the instantaneous power:

options.text: is negative for half the cycle
is constant at its peak value
reaches its maximum only at certain points and spends much time at zero or lower values
depends on the inductance of the load

blocks.explanation: Instantaneous power reaches its maximum only at certain points and spends significant time near zero, so the average is half the peak (17.2).

book_ref.quote: it spends significant time at zero or lower values

blocks.prompt: 28 A peak voltage of 100 V is applied across a 20 Ω resistor. The mean power is:

book_ref.quote: As the mean power is half of the maximum (peak) power

blocks.prompt: 29 The angle θ which specifies the instantaneous value of an alternating voltage or current is called its:
blocks.explanation: The angle which gives the value of an alternating quantity is called the phase (17.3).

book_ref.quote: The angle which gives the value of alternating quantity is known as phase.

blocks.prompt: 30 On one AC cycle, the point at which the phase is 3π/2 is where the voltage is:
blocks.explanation: Points A to E have phases 0, π/2, π, 3π/2 and 2π; at 3π/2, sin θ = −1, so the voltage is at its negative peak (17.3).

book_ref.quote: The phase of points A, B, C, D and E are 0, π/2, π, 3π/2 and 2π respectively

blocks.prompt: 31 The value of the phase angle at t = 0 is called the:
blocks.explanation: The phase angle at t = 0 is the initial phase of the AC quantity (17.3).

book_ref.quote: the value of the phase angle θ at t equals to zero is called the initial phase

blocks.prompt: 32 If V = Vₒ sin θ and I = Iₒ sin (θ + φ), then:

options.text: the current leads the voltage by φ
the current lags the voltage by φ
the voltage leads the current by φ

blocks.explanation: At t = 0, V = 0 but I = Iₒ sin φ is positive; the current reached zero earlier, so it leads by φ (17.3).

book_ref.quote: the current is leading the voltage by an angle φ in this situation

blocks.prompt: 33 V = Vₒ sin θ and I = Iₒ sin (θ − φ). At t = 0 (θ = 0), the current is:
blocks.explanation: Putting θ = 0 in I = Iₒ sin (θ − φ) gives I = −Iₒ sin φ; the current lags the voltage by φ (17.3, book correction).

book_ref.quote: current I is lagging behind the voltage V by an angle φ

blocks.prompt: 34 A current is I = 4 sin (θ + 30°) A while the voltage is V = 50 sin θ V. The current at θ = 0 is:
blocks.explanation: I = 4 sin 30° = 4 × 0.5 = 2 A; the current leads the voltage by 30° (17.3).

book_ref.quote: The angle φ is the phase difference between the voltage and the current.

blocks.prompt: 35 An alternating quantity can be represented by a vector that rotates:

options.text: anticlockwise at twice the angular frequency
anticlockwise with the angular frequency of the quantity
it does not rotate at all

blocks.explanation: The rotating vector turns anticlockwise with the same angular frequency as the alternating quantity (17.3).

book_ref.quote: An alternating quantity can be represented by an anticlockwise rotating vector

blocks.prompt: 36 The length of the rotating vector representing an alternating quantity shows its:
blocks.explanation: Its length on a scale represents the peak or rms value of the quantity (17.3).

book_ref.quote: Its length on a certain scale represents the peak value or rms value

blocks.prompt: 37 The rotating vector of an alternating quantity is horizontal at the instant when the quantity is:
blocks.explanation: It is horizontal when the alternating quantity is zero and increasing positively (17.3).

book_ref.quote: It is in horizontal position at the instant.

blocks.prompt: 38 The basic circuit elements in an AC circuit are:
blocks.explanation: In a DC circuit the basic element is a resistor; in AC circuits they are R, L and C (17.4).

book_ref.quote: The basic circuit element in a DC circuit is a resistor R

blocks.prompt: 39 In a DC circuit, the relation between current and voltage across a resistor is given by:
blocks.explanation: The resistor in a DC circuit obeys Ohm's law V = IR (17.4).

book_ref.quote: the relation between them is given by Ohm's law (V = IR)

blocks.prompt: 40 In a purely resistive AC circuit, the voltage and current are:
blocks.explanation: Both pass their maximum and minimum values at the same time, so they are in phase (17.5).

book_ref.quote: their instantaneous values are said to be in phase with each other

blocks.prompt: 41 A peak voltage of 240 V is applied across a 60 Ω resistor. The peak current is:

book_ref.quote: where Iₒ = Vₒ/R is the peak or maximum value of current.

blocks.prompt: 42 In the vector diagram for a resistor in an AC circuit, the vectors of V and I are drawn:
blocks.explanation: V and I are drawn parallel because there is no phase difference between them (17.5).

book_ref.quote: V and I are drawn parallel because there is no phase difference between them.

blocks.prompt: 43 An AC of peak value Iₒ produces less heating in a resistor than a DC of value Iₒ because the AC:

options.text: has a negative sign half the time
flows through the resistor only in one direction
is at its maximum value only for an instant in each half-cycle

blocks.explanation: Heating depends on I², not on the sign; but the AC is at Iₒ only for an instant in each half-cycle (17.5).

book_ref.quote: the alternating current is at this maximum value only for an instant during each half-cycle

blocks.prompt: 44 A 2 kW heater works on a 220 V supply. The current it takes is:
blocks.explanation: I = P/V = 2000 W/220 V = 9.09 A (17.5). Its resistance would be 220 V/9.09 A = 24.2 Ω.

book_ref.quote: It is to be noted that here P is measured in watts V in volts, I in amperes and R in ohms

blocks.prompt: 45 The relation P = VI for power holds good only when:

options.text: V and I are in phase

blocks.explanation: Eq. 17.12 for power holds only when V and I are in phase (17.5).

book_ref.quote: the Eq.(17.12) for power holds good only when V and I are in phase

blocks.prompt: 46 A doorbell is often run on 12 V AC because low-voltage AC:

options.text: is safer to handle and reduces the risk of shock
is converted to DC by the bell

blocks.explanation: Low-voltage AC is safer to handle and reduces the risk of electrical shock (17.5).

book_ref.quote: Low-voltage AC is safer to handle and reduces the risk of electrical shock.

blocks.prompt: 47 A heating element takes 5 A rms from a 230 V rms supply. Its average power is:

book_ref.quote: The opposition to AC which the circuit presents is the resistance given by

blocks.prompt: 48 An inductor (choke) is a component having:
blocks.explanation: An inductor is a passive two-terminal component with large self-inductance and negligible resistance (17.6).

book_ref.quote: a passive two terminal electrical component having a large value of self -inductance and negligible resistance

blocks.prompt: 49 An inductor slows down current surges by temporarily storing energy in:
blocks.explanation: The inductor slows surges by storing energy in an electromagnetic field and releasing it back into the circuit (17.6).

book_ref.quote: The inductor is used to slow down current surges or spikes

blocks.prompt: 50 In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current:

options.text: is in phase with the voltage

blocks.explanation: From V = Vₒ sin (ωt + π/2), the current lags the voltage by 90° or π/2 rad (17.6).

book_ref.quote: The current in an inductor always lags behind the voltage by 90° or π/2 rad.

blocks.prompt: 51 A coil of inductance 0.2 H is connected to a 50 Hz supply. Its inductive reactance is about:

book_ref.quote: inductive reactance X_L is directly proportional to both, frequency of current and the inductance L

blocks.prompt: 52 If the frequency of the supply to a pure inductor is doubled, its inductive reactance:
blocks.explanation: X_L = 2πfL is directly proportional to f, so doubling f doubles X_L (17.6).

book_ref.quote: In case of DC, f = 0, so X_L = 0, while in case of large AC frequency, X_L is also large.

blocks.prompt: 53 An ideal inductor:
blocks.explanation: For DC, f = 0 so X_L = 0, while X_L is large at high AC frequency; an inductor allows DC but blocks AC (17.6).

book_ref.quote: Thus, we conclude that an inductor allows DC but blocks the AC.

blocks.prompt: 54 The SI unit of inductive reactance is:
blocks.explanation: The unit of X_L is ohm (17.6).

book_ref.quote: allows DC but blocks the AC. The unit of X_L is ohm.

blocks.prompt: 55 The average power dissipated in a pure inductor over one cycle is:
blocks.explanation: A pure inductor stores energy in the magnetic field and returns it; the average power per cycle is zero (17.6).

book_ref.quote: The average power dissipated in a pure inductor is zero.

blocks.prompt: 56 Since an inductor does not consume energy, it is used for:
blocks.explanation: Since an inductor does not consume energy, it is used to control AC without consuming energy (17.6).

book_ref.quote: it is used for controlling AC without consuming energy

blocks.prompt: 57 A 0.25 H coil of negligible resistance carries an rms current of 20 mA at 500 Hz. The rms voltage across it is about:

book_ref.quote: A 400 mH coil of negligible resistance is connected to an AC circuit

blocks.prompt: 58 A choke is a coil of thick copper wire wound in a large number of turns over a:
blocks.explanation: A choke is wound closely with many turns of thick copper wire over a soft iron laminated core (17.7).

book_ref.quote: It is a coil of thick copper wire wound closely in a large number of turns over a soft iron laminated core.

blocks.prompt: 59 Because the resistance of a choke coil is negligibly small, its power factor is:
blocks.explanation: With negligible R, cos θ of the choke is almost zero and θ is nearly 90° (17.7).

book_ref.quote: the power factor (cosθ) of the choke coil is almost zero

blocks.prompt: 60 The phase difference between current and voltage in a choke coil is nearly:
blocks.explanation: For a choke θ is nearly 90°, so practically no power is dissipated as heat (17.7).

book_ref.quote: So practically, no power is dissipated as heat by a choke coil.

blocks.prompt: 61 The inductance of a choke coil is very high because of the:

options.text: high permeability of its iron core

blocks.explanation: The high permeability of the iron core makes the inductance L of the choke very high (17.7).

book_ref.quote: The inductance L of the choke coil is also very high due to the high permeability of iron core

blocks.prompt: 62 A choke is used to:

options.text: block high frequency AC while allowing DC and low frequency AC
block DC while allowing high frequency AC

blocks.explanation: A choke blocks high frequency AC while letting DC and low frequency AC pass (17.7).

book_ref.quote: Also choke is used to block high frequency AC while allowing DC and low frequency AC to pass.

blocks.prompt: 63 In a fluorescent light, the choke:

options.text: converts AC into DC for the tube
stores charge to light the tube
removes all current from the tube
generates transient voltages that help the gas reach breakdown

blocks.explanation: Chokes in fluorescent lights generate transient voltages across the tube, helping the breakdown of the gas (17.7).

book_ref.quote: Chokes in fluorescent lights generate transient voltages across the tube

blocks.prompt: 64 In switch-mode power supplies, choke coils help to:

options.text: regulate voltage and filter out switching noise
raise the frequency of the mains
store energy in an electric field

blocks.explanation: Choke coils are essential in switch-mode power supplies, regulating voltage and filtering switching noise (17.7).

book_ref.quote: They are essential in switch-mode power supplies

blocks.prompt: 65 A capacitor does not allow DC to pass because:

options.text: its plates are made of metal
its reactance is zero for DC
there is an insulating medium between its plates
it stores energy in a magnetic field

blocks.explanation: A capacitor blocks DC because of the insulating medium between its plates (17.8).

book_ref.quote: A capacitor does not allow direct current to pass through it

blocks.prompt: 66 A capacitor stores energy in the form of:
blocks.explanation: A capacitor stores energy in the form of an electric field, unlike a resistor (17.8).

book_ref.quote: a capacitor can store energy in the form of electric field

blocks.prompt: 67 Alternating current flows in a circuit containing a capacitor because:

options.text: the capacitor converts AC into DC
the capacitor charges in one direction and then the other, moving electrons to and fro

blocks.explanation: The capacitor charges one way then the other as the voltage reverses; electrons move to and fro around the circuit (17.8).

book_ref.quote: The result is that electrons move to and fro around the circuit

blocks.prompt: 68 In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the current:

options.text: is in phase with the voltage

blocks.explanation: I = Iₒ sin (ωt + π/2): the capacitor current leads the voltage by 90° (17.8, book correction: it is the capacitor, not the inductor).

book_ref.quote: Equations 17.18 and 17.19 show that inductor current I leads the voltage by 90°

blocks.prompt: 69 The capacitive reactance of a 20 μF capacitor at 50 Hz is about:

book_ref.quote: for low frequencies, capacitor will have a large reactance X_C and current I will be small

blocks.prompt: 70 If the frequency of the AC supply to a capacitor is increased, the current through it:
blocks.explanation: X_C = 1/2πfC falls as f rises, so the current through the same capacitor becomes large (17.8).

book_ref.quote: at high frequencies reactance X_C will be small and current I through the same capacitor will be large

blocks.prompt: 71 The scientist who pioneered the generation, transmission and use of alternating current was:
blocks.explanation: The box names Nikola Tesla, born 1856, as the father of alternating currents (17.8).

book_ref.quote: He pioneered the generation, transmission, and use of alternating current

blocks.prompt: 72 If the capacitance in a circuit is doubled at the same frequency, the capacitive reactance becomes:
blocks.explanation: X_C = 1/(2πfC) is inversely proportional to C, so doubling C halves X_C (17.8).

book_ref.quote: In electric circuits, a capacitor is a reactive component.

blocks.prompt: 73 The combined effect of resistance and reactances in an AC circuit is called:
blocks.explanation: The combined effect of resistance and reactances is impedance Z (17.9).

book_ref.quote: The combined effect of resistance and reactances in such circuits is known as impedance.

blocks.prompt: 74 An AC circuit has a peak voltage of 300 V and a peak current of 6 A. Its impedance is:

book_ref.quote: It is the ratio of the rms value of the voltage to the rms value of the current.

blocks.prompt: 75 The opposition to current flow due to capacitors and inductors is called:
blocks.explanation: Reactance is the opposition due to capacitors (X_C) and inductors (X_L) (17.9).

book_ref.quote: Reactance is the opposition to current flow due to capacitors

blocks.prompt: 76 The SI unit of impedance is:
blocks.explanation: Z = Vᵣₘₛ/Iᵣₘₛ, so its SI unit is ohm (17.9).

book_ref.quote: This SI unit of impedance is ohm.

blocks.prompt: 77 In an RC-series circuit, the quantity that is the same for R and C is the:
blocks.explanation: R and C are in series, so the same current flows through each (17.10).

book_ref.quote: As R and C are in series, so same current would flow through each of them.

blocks.prompt: 78 In an RC-series circuit, the voltage across the capacitor:

options.text: is in phase with the current
is in phase with the voltage across R

blocks.explanation: V_C = IᵣₘₛX_C lags behind the current by π/2 rad, so it is drawn at right angles to the current line (17.10).

book_ref.quote: As this, voltage lags behinds the current by π / 2 rad or 90°

blocks.prompt: 79 A 30 Ω resistor is in series with a capacitor of reactance 40 Ω. The impedance is:
blocks.explanation: Z = √(R² + X_C²) = √(30² + 40²) = 50 Ω, by vector addition (17.10).

book_ref.quote: Equation 17.21 suggests that we can find the impedance of a series AC circuit by vector addition.

blocks.prompt: 80 In an RC-series circuit with R = X_C, the current leads the applied voltage by:

book_ref.quote: the current is leading the voltage applied by the angle θ

blocks.prompt: 81 In an RC-series circuit, the power is consumed:
blocks.explanation: Power is consumed primarily by the resistor; the capacitor only stores energy and does not dissipate it (17.10).

book_ref.quote: as the capacitor only stores energy and does not dissipate it

blocks.prompt: 82 In the impedance diagram of an RC-series circuit, the reactance X_C is drawn:
blocks.explanation: R is along the current (reference); X_C = 1/ωC is drawn lagging the R line by 90°; Z is their vector sum (17.10).

book_ref.quote: Figure 17.9(c) is known as impedance diagram of the circuit.

blocks.prompt: 83 In an RL-series circuit, the voltage across the inductor:

options.text: is in phase with the current

blocks.explanation: V_L across L is ahead of the current by 90° (line OB); V_R is in phase with it (17.11).

book_ref.quote: As R and L are in series, therefore, same current I flows through both R and L.

blocks.prompt: 84 A 6 Ω resistor and a coil of reactance 8 Ω are in series. The impedance and phase angle are:

book_ref.quote: The angle θ which Z makes with R line, gives the phase difference

blocks.prompt: 85 An electric eel produces powerful shocks through specialised cells called:
blocks.explanation: Electric eels produce shocks through specialised cells called electrocytes (the box misprints 'electrolytes') (17.11).

book_ref.quote: Electric Eels create powerful shocks by its 3 main organs

blocks.prompt: 86 In P = VI cos θ, the factor cos θ is called the:
blocks.explanation: The factor cos θ is the power factor (17.11).

book_ref.quote: The factor cos θ is known as power factor.

blocks.prompt: 87 An RL-series circuit draws 5 A from a 220 V supply at a power factor of 0.8. The power consumed is:
blocks.explanation: P = VI cos θ = 220 V × 5 A × 0.8 = 880 W, all in the resistor (17.11).

book_ref.quote: as the inductor stores energy but ideally does not dissipate it

blocks.prompt: 88 A solar panel gives 400 W of DC power to an inverter of efficiency 90%. The AC power obtained is:
blocks.explanation: P_ac = (inverter efficiency) × P_dc = 0.90 × 400 W = 360 W (17.11).

book_ref.quote: we have to take an account of a quantity known as inverter efficiency

blocks.prompt: 89 The inverter efficiency usually lies in the range:
blocks.explanation: Inverter efficiency usually may be 85% to 90% (17.11).

book_ref.quote: It usually may be 85 % to 90%.

blocks.prompt: 90 In the impedance diagram of an RLC-series circuit, X_L and X_C are directed:
blocks.explanation: X_L = ωL and X_C = 1/ωC are directed opposite to each other (17.12).

book_ref.quote: are directed opposite to each other

blocks.prompt: 91 An RLC-series circuit has R = 40 Ω, X_L = 90 Ω and X_C = 60 Ω. Its impedance is:

book_ref.quote: The impedance of the RLC-series circuit is:

blocks.prompt: 92 At a very high frequency, an RLC-series circuit behaves like:

options.text: an open circuit with no current

blocks.explanation: At high frequency X_L = ωL ≫ X_C, so the inductive reactance dominates and the circuit behaves as RL-series (17.12).

book_ref.quote: so RLC-series circuit behaves as RL-series circuit

blocks.prompt: 93 At a very low frequency, the reactance that dominates in an RLC-series circuit is:
blocks.explanation: At low frequency X_C = 1/ωC ≫ X_L, so the circuit behaves as RC-series (17.12).

book_ref.quote: hence RLC series circuit behaves as RC series circuit

blocks.prompt: 94 Resonance occurs in an RLC-series circuit when:
blocks.explanation: At the frequency where X_L = X_C the reactances cancel; this condition is resonance (17.12).

book_ref.quote: This condition is called resonance.

blocks.prompt: 95 An RLC-series circuit has L = 0.1 H and C = 10 μF. Its resonance frequency is about:

book_ref.quote: The value of resonance frequency fᵣ can be obtained by applying the condition:

blocks.prompt: 96 At resonance, the impedance of an RLC-series circuit is:
blocks.explanation: At resonance the impedance is minimum, Z = R (17.12).

book_ref.quote: At resonance impedance, is minimum (Z = R)

blocks.prompt: 97 At resonance in an RLC-series circuit, the current is:

options.text: 90° out of phase with the voltage

blocks.explanation: Because the impedance is minimum, the current reaches its maximum value at resonance (17.12).

book_ref.quote: the current in the circuit reaches its maximum value due to the minimum impedance

blocks.prompt: 98 At resonance in an RLC-series circuit, the power factor is:
blocks.explanation: At resonance θ = 0, voltage and current are in phase and the power factor is 1 (17.12).

book_ref.quote: indicating that the voltage and current are in phase and have power factor equal to 1

blocks.prompt: 99 In an RLC-series circuit, increasing the resistance:

options.text: increases damping, so oscillations decay faster
makes the current at resonance larger

blocks.explanation: The resistor introduces damping; a higher resistance gives more damping and faster decay of oscillations (17.12).

book_ref.quote: A higher resistance leads to more damping

blocks.prompt: 100 In the car-spring analogy of an RLC-series circuit, the shock absorber corresponds to the:
blocks.explanation: The shock absorber damps the motion and dissipates energy, like the resistance (17.12).
